To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adherence of Lithuanian primary health care (PHC) physicians to the national guideline for type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) is low and the factors influencing better care are: a higher number of patients with diabetes, a higher proportion of patients with diabetes in the patient population, a higher proportion and number of patients with DM with microvascular complications, a longer time of working in a PHC, and a higher proportion of female patients.

the adherence to diabetes mellitus guideline recommendations was poor in Lithuanian primary health care (PHC) and the main barriers for better diabetes mellitus (DM) care are the lack of knowledge, lack of time, and the lack of motivation to follow the guideline.

the adherence to the guidelines for diabetes mellitus in PHC in Lithuania is not high, and the factors that influence it include the level of knowledge, the number of years of practice, and the availability of the necessary equipment.
